source: Q144 (2026-09-23): the owner's first named correction to the Z-Anatomy reference model -- the radial nerve pathway. Side-field union bug fix, name-map mapping fix, cited-literature audit of the Z-Anatomy radial nerve course, and one bounded, cited, declarative correction. CC BY-SA anatomy layer only (third_party/z-anatomy/NOTICE); no private/clinical content touched.

part_1_side_fix.bug: scripts/zanatomy/zan_source.py's load_source() restricted candidates by side only when the ATLAS id itself ended in _r/_l. Every nerve entity in this project's own registry (data/nerves/*.json) carries no side field at all (a known 'nerve-category data gap', Q142/Q143), so for these ids Z-Anatomy's own LEFT and RIGHT objects were both accepted and unioned into one mesh under the bare id -- radial_n shipped as one 14-component fragmented blob (Q143 finding).
part_1_side_fix.root_cause: this project's own registry does not split nerve entities by side (unlike muscles/bones, which are already stored as separate _r/_l entity records).
part_1_side_fix.fix: scripts/zanatomy/zan_source.py: when an unsided atlas_id's matched Z-Anatomy candidates include BOTH a 'right' and a 'left' object AND its category is 'nerve', ship two ids (<id>_r, <id>_l) instead of the bare id, each built only from its own side's candidates. Restricted to category=='nerve' (see part_1_audit below for why). No change to data/nerves/*.json, map_names.py, or the committed zanatomy_name_map.json -- the fix lives entirely in the Z-Anatomy-specific loader.
part_1_side_fix.note_on_6_components: still >1 because radial_n's own Z-Anatomy source unions genuinely distinct real sub-parts sharing one atlas_id ('Radial nerve.r' + 'Muscular branches of radial nerve.r', separate motor branch stubs to the triceps heads etc. -- the multi-part-union behaviour Q142 built for e.g. extensor_carpi_ulnaris_r's two heads) -- not a left/right union artifact any more.

audit_of_other_bilateral_ids_with_the_sa.method: For every atlas_id with no _r/_l suffix, checked whether its confident/exact-matched Z-Anatomy candidates span both a 'right' and a 'left' object (the exact condition that produces the union bug).
audit_of_other_bilateral_ids_with_the_sa.confirms_PROJECT_STATE_Q142_Q143_note: sciatic_n and femoral_n, flagged there by name only as carrying 'the same data gap', are both confirmed on this list to carry the exact same union bug -- now fixed by the same generic change.

non_nerve_category_ids_and_why_left_alon.ethmoid: bone -- Z-Anatomy ships this single physical bone's own left/right labyrinth halves as two objects; unioning them IS the correct single-entity behaviour, not a side-independence bug.
non_nerve_category_ids_and_why_left_alon.external_anal_sphincter: muscle -- one midline sphincter ring, modelled as two half-ring objects; unioning is correct.
non_nerve_category_ids_and_why_left_alon.procerus: muscle -- a midline muscle with two fused bellies; unioning is correct.
non_nerve_category_ids_and_why_left_alon.interclavicular_ligament: ligament -- one ligament spanning both clavicles; unioning is correct.
non_nerve_category_ids_and_why_left_alon.intertransverse_ligament: ligament -- this project's one id covers the paired ligaments at every vertebral level as a single combined entity; unioning is correct.

audit_of_other_bilateral_ids_with_the_sa.why_the_fix_is_restricted_to_category_ne: a nerve is never one structure across both sides (radial_n_r and radial_n_l are two independent nerves), unlike the 5 ids above where Z-Anatomy's own left/right split is a MESH-authoring artifact of one real combined structure. Confirmed by inspection of every one of the 5 non-nerve ids above, not assumed.

part_2_name_map_bug_found_while_auditing.bug: 'Deep branch of radial nerve' (the posterior interosseous nerve) scored a confident 0.90 match to `radial_n` (the trunk) instead of this project's own dedicated `posterior_interosseous_n` entity, because the generic substring scorer favours 'radial nerve' (a substring of the Z-Anatomy name) over 'posterior interosseous nerve' (no shared tokens). Left uncorrected, `posterior_interosseous_n` shipped with ZERO geometry and the PIN's own mesh was folded into the trunk.
part_2_name_map_bug_found_while_auditing.fix: a small by-name override in zan_source.py (_ATLAS_ID_OVERRIDE), the same precedent as Q142's three prior fixes -- map_names.py and the committed zanatomy_name_map.json are untouched.
part_2_name_map_bug_found_while_auditing.effect: posterior_interosseous_n now ships (as posterior_interosseous_n_r/_l, via the side-split fix above) with its own real Z-Anatomy geometry ('Deep branch of radial nerve.r/.l'), separate from the trunk.

part_3_pathway_audit.method: Full method: data/corrections/zanatomy/radial_n.json's own 'method' field. Summary: per-Y-bin centroid centreline of each nerve mesh (right side; left independently re-measured and found to mirror EXACTLY -- both sides gave identical numbers), nearest-vertex distance (scipy cKDTree) to bone/muscle meshes, and trimesh.Trimesh.contains() point-in-mesh containment for the supinator entry/exit (more rigorous than a nearest-vertex threshold). All measurements in mm, offset from the lateral epicondyle (fit live from this build's own Humerus.r/.l mesh), positive = proximal, negative = distal. Z-Anatomy humerus length (both sides): 317.6mm.
part_3_pathway_audit.landmarks: see data/corrections/zanatomy/radial_n.json's own `landmarks` array for the full table (measured, cited range, citation, status) -- reproduced in summary form in the PROJECT_STATE.md Q144 entry and the final report.
citations: Carlan D, Pratt J, Patterson JMM, Weiland AJ, Boyer MI, Gelberman RH (2007). The radial nerve in the brachium: an anatomic study in human cadavers. J Hand Surg Am 32(8):1177-82. PMID 17923300, DOI 10.1016/j.jhsa.2006.07.001.
Jain RK, Champawat VS, Mandlecha P (2018). Danger zone of radial nerve in Indian population -- a cadaveric study. J Clin Orthop Trauma 10(3):531-534. PMID 31061584, DOI 10.1016/j.jcot.2018.02.006.

Artico M, Telera S, Tiengo C, Stecco C, Macchi V, Porzionato A, Vigato E, Parenti A, De Caro R (2008). Surgical anatomy of the radial nerve at the elbow. Surg Radiol Anat 31(2):101-6. PMID 18795220, DOI 10.1007/s00276-008-0412-8.

Aggarwal N, Maurya R, Tiwari V, Pathak A, Chaudhary P (2026). Surface landmark-based estimation of the posterior interosseous nerve: a cadaveric anatomical study. Hand Surg Rehabil, in press. PMID 42556533, DOI 10.1016/j.hansur.2026.102756.
Hazani R, Engineer NJ, Mowlavi A, Neumeister M, Lee WPA, Wilhelmi BJ (2008). Anatomic landmarks for the radial tunnel. Eplasty 8:e37. PMID 18668182.

Beldner S, Zlotolow DA, Melone CP, Agnes AM, Jones MH (2005). Anatomy of the lateral antebrachial cutaneous and superficial radial nerves in the forearm: a cadaveric and clinical study. J Hand Surg Am 30(6):1226-30. PMID 16344180, DOI 10.1016/j.jhsa.2005.07.004.

shift_sweep_for_pin_entry_correction_mm.note: post-warp, post-bone-avoidance-safety-pass entry level (mm distal to LE) for a sweep of the anchor's nominal shift -- plateaus well short of the cited range for every value tried, see data/corrections/zanatomy/radial_n.json's own avoid_penetration_note.

part_4_correction_applied.wired_into: scripts/zanatomy/build_zan_reference.py (applied on the raw atlas-frame mesh before the hip-origin subtraction, matched-entity loop)
part_4_correction_applied.landmark_corrected: PIN entry into supinator (arcade of Frohse)
part_4_correction_applied.residual_gap_reason: this build's own mandatory bone-avoidance safety pass (Radius) caps how far a Y-only warp can move this point without running the nerve through bone -- see data/corrections/zanatomy/radial_n.json's own note; a full match would need a small lateral (X/Z) path adjustment, out of scope for this bounded 1-D correction.

recheck_after_correction.note: components measured on the corrected (posterior_interosseous_n) mesh alone, before vs after the warp+push-off -- 1 component both times (this branch object itself was never fragmented; the 14->6 fragmentation fix is the radial_n TRUNK id, part 1 above).

landmarks_not_corrected.a_spiral_groove_contact: within cited range (Carlan et al. 2007) -- not corrected.
landmarks_not_corrected.b_septum_piercing: within cited range (Artico et al. 2008 / Jain et al. 2018) -- not corrected.
landmarks_not_corrected.c_elbow_position: qualitatively confirmed anterior to humerus, between brachialis and brachioradialis -- not corrected.
landmarks_not_corrected.d_bifurcation_level: measured ~8mm distal to LE, ~1mm distal to this model's own radial head level -- textbook-consistent but no cadaveric mm citation found; marked unsourced, not corrected.
landmarks_not_corrected.e_pin_supinator_exit: within cited range (Aggarwal et al. 2026 / Hazani et al. 2008) -- not corrected, kept as a fixed anchor.
landmarks_not_corrected.f_superficial_branch_under_brachioradial: qualitatively consistent with Beldner et al. 2005; the specific transition distance could not be independently verified with the available geometry proxy (nearest-vertex distance cannot distinguish deep vs. superficial position) -- not corrected.

tests: tests/test_zanatomy_corrections.py (6 new tests: bump_warp_y anchors/clamping, monotonicity/no-fold, load_corrections finds the radial_n file, empty-directory no-op, apply_correction no-op for an uncorrected id, correction file structural well-formedness).

bundle_rebuild.coverage_recount_fix: scripts/zanatomy/verify_zan_reference.py's own entity-coverage recount matched bundle ids to registry ids EXACTLY, so the side-split (radial_n -> radial_n_r/_l) silently undercounted coverage for every one of the 64 split ids (302 -> a wrong 243) until fixed to also match <id>_r/<id>_l -- a real regression this task's own required re-check caught and fixed, not left as a known issue.
